json.row_subtitle: fields title / subtitle / thumb come from a C++ binder
json.intro: This page walks through the view-description JSON one layer at a time: each step is the previous JSON plus a small addition, and the view below is built from that JSON.
json.step1_note: The smallest possible JSON: a type plus one attribute.
json.step2_note: Adds Box (axis/gap) + children - this is how the view tree grows.
json.step3_note: Adds padding, corner radius, background color and grow - size and looks live in JSON.
json.step4_note: Adds theme lookups (@theme/...) and a percentage width - a theme switch updates them.
json.step5_note: Adds Image + @res/... (paths are relative to the resources directory).
json.step6_note: Adds @i18n/... instead of hard-coded text, plus font size from the theme.
json.step7_note: Adds include: the structure moves to another file, the main file keeps one line.
json.step8_note: Finally: one template instantiated many times, values filled in by C++ via bind fields.
json.step7_text: This content comes from another file (included).
json.failed: This JSON failed to build a view (see the log)
json.demo_intro: This page splits JSON into two things: what each layer looks like on its own, and how view transitions are written. Every row below is rendered from theme JSON, not a screenshot.
json.layers_hint: The sample card stacks five layers. Each row below shows only one of them (theme-side: import + paint the others transparent), so you can see what each layer does.
json.layer_shadow: shadow - the drop shadow (before the fill, outer ring only)
json.layer_hlbg: hlBg - highlight background (focus; must sit before the content)
json.layer_icon: icon - icon layer (source: icon uses the icon font automatically)
json.layer_title: title - text layer (source: text; inset leaves room for the icon)
json.composite_hint: All five layers together - order is shadow > bg > hlBg > icon > title.
json.anim_title: 3) Animations, one channel at a time
json.anim_hint: Each card replays its own enter every 1.6s, all driven by the same ViewTransition (draw-time transforms only, so zero relayout during the animation).
json.anim_translatex: translateX - slide in from the left
json.anim_translatey: translateY - drop in from the top
json.anim_after: layer + when: after - the title surfaces only after the card lands (offsetY + opacity)
json.extension_row: Extension layer: the op is registered by a third party (see demo/contrib/stripe_layer.cpp); the appearance is inlined here
json.quad_row: Second extension layer: four vertices wander independently (demo/contrib/quad_layer.cpp; all 7 params come from the declared schema)
json.children_row: children: one appearance is a complete control (the structure lives in JSON, zero C++)

theme.hint: Appearance comes from resources/theme/<name>/widgets/*.json: draw structure (background/border/text) and state animation (tweeny interpolation) all live in JSON. Copy default, rename, edit JSON - that is a new skin.
theme.widgets_desc: Rectangle and Button contain no drawing code at all - background, radius, text and colors all come from JSON.
theme.states_desc: Move focus with left/right, watch the color tween; press A to see the press feedback.
theme.dialog_desc: Backdrop and panel are appearance-driven: opacity and offset tweens live in JSON. While open, input is modal - clicks outside and arrow keys do not reach the page below, and focus returns to the button that opened it.
theme.dialog_demo_text: Panel, title, body and button placement all come from theme JSON. Try clicking outside: it will not pass through.
theme.input_desc: Desktop uses inline typing (characters / backspace / arrows / Enter to accept / Esc to cancel); Switch pops the system keyboard (swkbd). Editing is a standalone text model, so CJK is deleted by character.

nav.hint: TabFrame: tab bar + content area; switching detaches the old page instead of destroying it.
nav.body_a: Switch away and back - this page is not rebuilt.
nav.body_b: Content is provided by the caller; TabFrame only handles switching and appearance.
nav.body_c: Tab cell appearance comes from widgets/tab_cell.json in the theme.
nav.event_hint: The framework publishes focus/action events; this line updates live and resets after 3s (via task::delay, cancelling the previous timer).

page.json_sub: A whole screen described in JSON
page.settings_sub: List cells: detail / bool / radio / selector / slider / input
page.transform_sub: Draw-time scale / rotate / skew / translate + eased tweens
page.icons_sub: All glyphs of both icon fonts: 10 per row, code below

text.hint: Font sizes and colors come from the theme: they follow skin switches and window size (sizes are authored for 720p).
text.truncate_desc: Truncated with an ellipsis when too narrow; the one below is limited to 280px.
text.long: This is a fairly long line of text used to show truncation and wrapping.
text.live_sample: This text is resized, aligned and truncated live by the cells above.

layout.hint: Yoga/Flexbox: main axis, cross axis, grow, percentage sizes.
layout.grow_desc: 80px fixed on the left, grow takes the rest.

list.hint: 1000 items; rows leaving the viewport go back to a pool and are reused.

overlay.hint: Overlays and modal input: input becomes modal while open (clicks outside and arrows do not pass through), and focus returns afterwards.

settings.hint: The whole page is made of cells. Space/Enter toggles switches and radios, left/right changes selectors.
settings.status_note: Bottom right: battery, network and clock. On desktop there is no hardware, so demo data is injected; Switch reads psm/nifm.
settings.switch_style_hint: borealis renders switches as an on/off label with a font bounce (above); this is our extra style via setStyle(BooleanCellStyle::SWITCH).

transform.hint: The box below never triggers a relayout - transforms only affect drawing.

scroll.hint: The card above holds an independent scroller; the buttons below verify scroll-to-focus.
scroll.paragraph: Paragraph {}: the scroller has its own content height and indicator; focus scrolls it into view.

pokedex.hint: Two sections. Headers use a registered section_header cell; each section has its own cell type. Press A for detail, B to go back. Sprites are Nintendo IP, so we self-draw a type-colored placeholder.

shadow.hint: A shadow is a layer: {"op": "shadow", "fill": color, "feather": blur, "offset": [x,y], "radius": corner, "spread": expansion}. Put it before your background layer to draw it first.
shadow.quality_hint: fast = 8 layers (default, cheap); smooth = 24 gaussian-weighted layers. Or set BKLV_SHADOW_QUALITY=smooth before launch.
shadow.variant_hint: Same appearance, different variant file — no code change.
shadow.params_hint: Feather/offset/radius/color all live in the widget JSON; shadows also support state animations (e.g. deeper shadow.opacity on focus).
shadow.cutout_hint: With "cutout": true on a shadow layer, only the outer ring is drawn (the widget rect is punched out), so a translucent background will not reveal the shadow. The two cards share the same translucent fill.
shadow.inner_title: Inner shadow: add "inner": true to a shadow layer
shadow.card_inner: Inner shadow (darkest at the edge, fading inward, symmetric)
shadow.card_inner_glow: A light color turns it into an inner glow
shadow.inner_hint: Inner and outer shadows are the same shadow layer, just a boolean apart. Outer shadows sit behind the control (hoisted to the front while parsing); inner shadows paint above the fill in written order, have no direction (offset does not apply), fade inward from the edge, and never leave the shape.

icons.title: Icons
icons.missing: Icon font not found, glyphs will show as boxes

base_widgets.hint: Everything here is composed from theme JSON: edit base/ and every derived widget follows.
base_widgets.selector_hint: Press a selector to enter edit mode: focus is pinned, L/R adjusts, holding repeats; press again to exit.
base_widgets.label_body: Body text: follows color.text.primary and the theme font size
base_widgets.label_dim: Secondary text: color.text.dim, used for hints
base_widgets.label_long: This line is deliberately very long so you can see single-line truncation (it becomes an ellipsis)
base_widgets.label_hint: Label is code-driven: wrapping, truncation, line height and font are set in C++.
base_widgets.image_hint: Async decode + texture upload; size comes from the layout (fixed 120x120 here).
base_widgets.slider_hint: Colors, radius and thickness come from base/slider.json; where the progress is drawn is C++.
base_widgets.spinner_hint: Left spins in 1.2s, right in 2.4s (duration and thickness are set in code).
base_widgets.states_hint: Each state row is a separate instance with setAppearanceState() applied (nothing is really clicked); the names come from the theme JSON.
base_widgets.info_hint: Click the 'interactive' button above: its info text becomes the click count.
base_widgets.switch_hint: The on/off states carry tweens (knob offset); click the 'interactive' one to see the animation.
base_widgets.dropdown_hint: Dropdowns and selectors have no extra states to show, so only the control itself is shown.
base_widgets.icon_hint: Both are 48x48: the square uses component.radius, the circle uses radius.round (=999) on all four layers; the icon layer is align/valign center, so it is truly centered.
base_widgets.list_hint: The list-element flavour of the plain button: widget/button.list drops the border (transparent bg.stroke + strokeWidth 0) and left-aligns the text; size, padding and states stay the same as the plain button.
base_widgets.box_gradient: Gradient fill (same rect layer, gradient instead of a solid)

shell.intro: These three switches drive shell-level state (header / footer / log window). They used to sit above every page; now they live here.
shell.bars_hint: Hidden means GONE - it takes no space and content expands.
shell.debug_hint: The log window is a real view (no view per line) and never takes focus.
